'''''Ridolfia segetum''''', called '''false fennel''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''corn parsley''', or '''false caraway''', is an annual weed of the Mediterranean region. Its height is {{Convert|40|-|100|cm|in}}. The stem is erect, [[Striate (botany)|striate]], and branched. The [[Glabrousness#In_botany|glabrous]] leaves are finely divided several times with [[Glossary_of_botanical_terms#filiform|filiform]] leaflets.  The upper leaves frequently reduced and the base of the petiole enlarged. The flowers are yellow, arranged in small umbels with almost uniform rays (10–60).

The seeds and leaves contain an [[essential oil]] and the plant has a strong odor. The essential oil contains the chemicals [[α-phellandrene]], [[Terpinene|α-terpinolene]], [[phellandrene|β-phellandrene]], and [[dillapiol]].<ref>{{cite journal  |vauthors=Bicchi C, Rubiolo P, Ballero M, etal |title=HIV-1-inhibiting activity of the essential oil of Ridolfia segetum and Oenanthe crocata |journal=Planta Medica |volume=75 |issue=12 |pages=1331–5 | date=October 2009 |pmid=19347799 |doi=10.1055/s-0029-1185546|s2cid=9813693 }}</ref>

The leaves can be eaten in its raw form or cooked,<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Lentini F, Venza F |title=Wild food plants of popular use in Sicily |journal=J Ethnobiol Ethnomed |volume=3 |pages=15 |year=2007 |pmid=17397527 |pmc=1858679 |doi=10.1186/1746-4269-3-15 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and are used as an herb in the pickle industry.
